Definition: from a presumed compound of G2756 and G5456; empty sounding, i.e. fruitless discussion:--vain.
BiblicalUsage: Kenophonia means empty sounding, vain babbling, fruitless talk. 1 Timothy 6:20 tells Timothy to avoid profane and vain babblings, and 2 Timothy 2:16 says shun them, for they will increase unto more ungodliness.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe empty talk is never harmless: it grows, and what it grows into is more ungodliness.
